commonMistakes: Mitosis does not produce four genetically different cells; that is associated with meiosis.

detailedExplanation: The nucleus contains chromosomes, which are made from DNA. Each chromosome carries many genes. In body cells, chromosomes are normally found in pairs.

Cells divide through a sequence called the cell cycle. Before a cell divides it grows and increases the number of sub-cellular structures such as mitochondria and ribosomes. Its DNA is replicated so there are two copies of each chromosome. During mitosis, one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end and the nucleus divides. Finally the cytoplasm and cell membrane divide, producing two genetically identical daughter cells.
Mitosis is important for growth, repair and replacement of cells and for asexual reproduction in some organisms.
TGS explicitly states that detailed meiosis is not taught at this point; students only need to be aware that meiosis exists and will be studied later.
You must know what chromosomes and genes are and describe the overall stages of the cell cycle including mitosis.
